trickyParts: The answer part must be replaced, not reworded: itemblocks.Align's rule 3 would hand a second answer the first answer's id, since both sit after the last option with type answer. AlignReplaced skips rule 3 for the named types, so a replaced answer becomes a removed part and the new one mints its own id.

A part's identity hash is salted with its type (itemblocks.Hash(type + "\n" + text)): matchKey matches on the hash alone, so an option whose text equalled the question's would otherwise take the question's id.

refs.Stamp was missing on three ask paths that never wrote references before (closeAskTx, docs.answerApprovalAsk, restoreIssueAsksTx). Without it an answer's new part edges carry source_seq null and are invisible to a ?since= read. Added, with a test.

refs.Closure reads the refs table alone and its doc comment claimed every item keeps its own refs row beside its blocks' mentions. An ask keeps one for its question alone, so a document linked only from an option never joined its issue's closure. Closed with an anchor arm over ask_block_refs whose via is the ask.

discoveredComplexity: An ask's reads and its mutation answers differ by design: a read carries each option's part id and the ask's revision (batched beside the backlink counts), a mutation's answer carries neither, as it carries no referenced_by_count. Anything comparing the two compares the option text.

ask_block is a storage kind an older build does not know, so a build without these tables skips every ask-part row rather than mis-resolving it; TestAnOlderBuildSkipsItemBlockRows pins that for all three item kinds.

The simplify pass generalized four single-caller refs wrappers into refs.ItemBlockAt and refs.RemovedItemBlockNode, which four prose citations name; a later slice adding a fourth item kind extends those rather than adding wrappers.
